name: SheetCheck
tagline: Catch broken spreadsheet templates before a customer does
short: Upload an .xlsx and get a pass/fail report in seconds: dead formulas, #REF! errors, empty tabs, and sheets that are really just tables pretending to be tools.
medium: SheetCheck opens your spreadsheet template, recalculates it, and tells you if it actually works. It counts real formulas, measures density, finds every #REF! and #DIV/0!, and flags empty tabs. If your 'automated budget tracker' has 11 formulas across 3,000 cells, you find out before a buyer does.
long: Every digital-product seller has shipped a broken spreadsheet at least once. The file opens, it's the right size, the tabs are named correctly — and three months later a refund request arrives because the totals never calculated. File size is not evidence that a product works. SheetCheck is the check that runs before you list. Upload an .xlsx and get back a pass/fail verdict with the numbers behind it: how many real formulas exist, formula density per cell, every error literal (#REF!, #DIV/0!, #VALUE!, #NAME?, #N/A, #NULL!, #NUM!), empty or orphaned sheets, and corrupt workbook members. It recalculates the workbook headlessly so it reads computed values, not cached ones — the difference between a formula that looks fine in the XML and a formula that actually errors when a buyer opens it. Built for people selling spreadsheet templates on Etsy, Gumroad, Payhip and Creative Market, where a single broken formula costs a review, a refund, and the listing's ranking. Run it on one file or a whole folder before every launch.
pricing: Freemium — 3 free checks, then $9 one-time for unlimited local use

_build_status.engine: EXISTS — tools/etsy-listing-tool/qa_products.py + qa_compute.py, working, already caught a real failure (Social-Media-Content-Planner: 11 formulas / 3,016 cells)
_build_status.missing: web wrapper + payment (later). CLI is LIVE and public.
_build_status.buildable_by_us_at_zero_cost: CLI packaging, docs, landing copy, submission pack
_build_status.needs_greg: nothing for the free CLI — it is published. Storefront account only when the paid version exists.

_first_10_users: r/Etsy and r/EtsySellers (account-age gated — needs a real account), Etsy seller Facebook groups, the 'digital products' Gumroad discord, and the RIP-list content format: 'RIP broken spreadsheet listings' targeting a genuinely hated problem. NOT paid ads.
_kill_criteria: 0 paying users 30 days after the first directory listing goes live → kill and reuse the QA engine internally only. 1-3 users → keep listed, stop promoting. 4+ → build the web version.
_why_this_one_first: The engine already exists and has already caught a real defect. Nobody else sells spreadsheet-template QA specifically — the niche is unserved rather than crowded. And per the Single-Job Rule it is one job, named for the job, sold to a named buyer.
